# Query groups

*Feature* · also written query group

A Search Console Insights feature that groups similar queries together so their clicks can be read as one topic.

**Glossary** (*Query groups*): Search Console groups of queries with very similar intent written differently, computed with AI and titled with the most prominent query. Shown in Search Console Insights for properties with many queries; they do not affect ranking.

13 claims mention it: 1 from Google's documentation, 10 shown or said at the event (1 not in Google docs, 2 confirmed by Google docs, 5 consistent with Google docs, 2 nothing to verify), 2 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Introducing Query groups in Search Console Insights](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/10/search-console-query-groups).

- [`D3-C463`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Docs: Google's query groups announcement (27 October 2025) says the groups are computed with AI, may change over time and do not affect ranking, and that query groups are available only to properties with a large volume of queries. `[D3-C463, docs, Search Central blog (27 October 2025), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/10/search-console-query-groups]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D3-C418`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Google named granularity as a design challenge of query groups: putting many queries into one large group versus splitting them into smaller, more specific groups. `[D3-C418, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C413`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Search Console's query groups put together queries that express a very similar user intent but are written differently, for example with more or fewer words or with spelling errors, so site owners can see the intent behind their traffic instead of every query string. `[D3-C413, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C449`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Platform properties also show the query groups that lead to the account's content and the countries that send it traffic. `[D3-C449, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C417`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google said query groups are not built by matching query text alone: deciding which queries belong in which group goes beyond simple text filtering. `[D3-C417, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C419`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Query groups can change when the meaning of a query changes over time: a 2023 search for 'Gemini' may have meant the astrological sign, but after Google launched Gemini it means something else, so Search Console may now group it differently. `[D3-C419, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C421`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Query groups appear in the Search Console Insights report as a table of the top groups, showing the total clicks of all the queries inside each group, with an option to view a larger table. `[D3-C421, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C422`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Each query group in Search Console is titled with the most prominent query in the group. `[D3-C422, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C423`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Drilling into a query group opens the Search Console Performance report with a regex filter that contains all the queries of the group, so each individual query can be analysed. `[D3-C423, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C412`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, nothing to verify: Google's Search Console talk at the Deep Dive covered five Search Console launches of the past year: query groups, AI-powered configuration of the Performance report, generative AI control and reporting, platform properties for social accounts, and multimodal search reporting. `[D3-C412, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C424`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Stage, Day 3, nothing to verify: Google's Search Console team said query groups have been found very useful and that people are using them. `[D3-C424, stage, Ariel Kroszynski, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D3-C426`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Analysis: The speaker placed the query groups launch, hedging, in December, but Google's announcement is dated 27 October 2025 with a gradual rollout over the following weeks, so many sites may first have seen the card around December 2025. `[D3-C426, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C427`](../sessions/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) Analysis: For content planning, read query groups (and their trending up and trending down views) as intent themes: write for the intent the group stands for, not for each spelling or phrasing variant in it. `[D3-C427, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
